newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: British tourist killed by "robotic" attacker.
newsitem.headline: British tourist killed by "robotic" attacker.

text.p: One of the men who kicked and punched a British tourist to death at Bondi Beach was "robotic", the dead man's girlfriend said on Sunday at an emotional news conference called to urge witnesses to come forward.
Brian Hagland, 28, was beaten to death on Saturday in front of his girlfriend Connie Casey, 25, who frantically fought the two attackers, hitting them with her bag and screaming for help.
"The man who attacked Brian, I could tell he was dangerous, that he was going to do something...and I said to Brian don't look at him," a weeping Casey told reporters.
"His eyes were glazed, he was robotic. It was like he didn't even see Brian, he was looking through Brian, but he needed someone to take his anger out on," she said.

The attack early on Saturday in a well-lit, busy street just off Campbell Parade, the main street along the beach. Hagland and Casey had just got off a bus and were walking home to a nearby flat when the two men attacked.
Casey said one of the men, whom she said was Australian, taunted Hagland for carrying a bunch of flowers that had been presented to her by her workmates earlier that evening.
"He said "Come on, let's have it'," Casey said. "Then his friend stood back and he punched Brian and dragged him to the ground."
"They just picked him off the street and they killed him. I kept shouting to get off him. He didn't stand a chance," wept Casey.
Hagland was treated by ambulance at the scene and taken to hospital, but died of extensive head and internal injuries.

Police on Sunday issued two sketches of Hagland's attackers, both in their mid-20s, and asked doctors to report anyone seeking treatment for a bad cut or cuts as they believe a trail of blood from the scene to the beach was left by one of the men.
Casey and Hagland had been in Australia for eight months and had been due to leave for New Zealand in a few weeks.
The couple were using compensation money Casey had recently received after she was attacked in a London jewellers two years ago, she said.
"We were planning to marry," Casey said. "We had it all mapped out. We'd get engaged in Tahiti and marry in England."
